subject: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orbithealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@orbithealth.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Per our mutual action plan (attached: Orbit_Health_MAP_v3.xlsx) I captured three options for the production path and a recommended sequencing for region cutovers. High-level:

- Option A: Hosted -> scale in us-west, low-friction, fastest time-to-value.
- Option B: Dedicated reserved capacity (us-west + us-east failover) – predictable throughput, better data isolation.
- Option C: Private VPC (on-prem or customer-managed cloud) – compliance-first, longer lead time.

Two asks for you this week so we can lock timelines:
1) Confirm if Orbit requires an on-prem/private deployment for initial go-live (regulatory constraint) or if Dedicated is acceptable.
2) Confirm preferred go-live region (us-west primary vs. us-east primary).

We suggested a canary in us-west, then regional rollouts; the MAP contains milestones with rough lead times for Dedicated and Private paths. If you can review and mark the preferred option in the MAP spreadsheet by Wednesday, we’ll prepare the SOW and procurement path.

Attachments: Orbit_Health_MAP_v3.xlsx, Orbit_SOW_hosting_drafts.docx

Thanks —

Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orbithealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing

Thanks Dylan — excellent capture. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Compliance note: our security team flagged that certain PHI processing must be isolated to our VPC by policy for the first 6 months. That pushes us away from Hosted for initial go-live unless there is a strong compensating control.
- Timeline: target pilot launch week of 2027-08-09.

Two asks back to you:
1) Can you provide a short write-up of what Dedicated + VPC isolation would look like operationally and the expected procurement timeline?
2) Any chance you can produce a firm quote for Dedicated capacity (3x p3-equivalent) and a separate SOW for Private deployment?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will get procurement looped for contract timing.

—Samira
VP, Product & Integrations | Orbit Health
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing

Dylan — forwarding Samira's notes. Quick internal sync items:

- Procurement window: if they need Private for pilot, procurement + infra provisioning likely 8–10 weeks; Dedicated with reserved capacity ~2–3 weeks (assuming PO).
- Cost delta: Dedicated ~1.6x hosted on a per-token basis when fully utilized; Private carries upfront infra and networking costs (estimate in redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf).
- Risk: If we push them into Private now, we lose quick telemetry for early-quality tuning. Consider proposing a hybrid: Dedicated in a customer VPC (private tenancy) — reduces lead time and satisfies isolation for PHI.

Action: Karthik / Lauren, can you produce a short one-pager (bullet) for Samira that outlines the hybrid Dedicated-in-VPC option plus procurement steps? I can draft SOW language once we agree on sequencing.

-Grace
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing

Grace / team —

Attached is a concise bullets doc I pulled together for Samira (see Orbit_SOW_hosting_drafts.docx and redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf). Summary to include in reply:

- Hybrid path (Recommended): Deploy Dedicated capacity in customer-managed VPC (us-west primary). Benefits: meets PHI isolation, faster than full Private, still supports our standard observability and rollouts.
- Procurement steps: 1) PO for Reserved Capacity (2–3 weeks), 2) VPC peering and firewall rules (1–2 weeks), 3) initial canary + validation (1 week).
- Pricing: initial reserve (3x p3-equivalent) + setup fee; see redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf.

Can someone in leadership sign off on a one-time credit to accelerate pilot (staggered billing, common ask for customers in regulated industries)? If yes, we can close to their target pilot date (2027-08-09).

Karthik
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing

Looping in leadership approval note: I ran the ask with finance — we can approve a one-time pilot credit equivalent to 4 weeks of Dedicated capacity (value ~USD 28,000) if the customer signs the SOW and commits to a 12-month reserved term within 30 days of pilot completion.

I'll draft the short approval memo for legal and procurement to include a clear clause tying the credit to the reserved term. Grace, please add the clause into the SOW draft. Once we have Samira's selection on hybrid vs Private, we'll generate the final SOW and the DocuSign envelope.

-Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orbithealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbit Health MAP: hosting tie-break & region sequencing

Thanks all — that hybrid Dedicated-in-VPC approach looks like the right middle ground. Orbit will:

- Accept the hybrid deployment path as recommended.
- Target pilot go-live week: 2027-08-09 (us-west primary).
- Procurement will issue a PO for the reserved capacity by 2027-06-30 if SOW & pricing match the quoted terms.

Please send the finalized SOW and DocuSign link; procurement@orbithealth.com will countersign on receipt. We appreciate the proposed pilot credit — helps make this faster.

Samira
VP, Product & Integrations | Orbit Health
